notes: Baseline went deeper than iteration-1: explicit mix-vs-rate decomposition (Kitagawa-style), Simpson's paradox named. Missed only on recommendation format (no confidence grades).
With-skill pass rate is 30/30 (100%) vs baseline 26/30 (86.7%) — +13.3pp absolute improvement. Reproduces the iteration-1 headline cleanly with a fair timing comparison.

Honest timing tradeoff: with_skill is ~16% slower (+151s mean) and uses ~20% more tokens (+24k mean). The skill's Phases 3 (Validate) and 6 (Deliver quality bar) add real compute cost, and the deliverables are measurably richer in return.

All 4 baseline failures are on the same two themes: owner+confidence-graded recommendations (3 of 4) and explicit arithmetic re-derivation (1 of 4). Both are exactly what the skill's Phases 3 and 6 teach. The assertions discriminate well.

Baseline quality improved materially between iterations. Iteration-1 baseline was 25/30 (83.3%); iteration-2 is 26/30 (86.7%). Notably, Eval-1 baseline now gets action-titled charts (missed in iteration-1) and Eval-3 baseline now does a formal mix-vs-rate decomposition. This suggests the with_skill vs baseline gap is a floor, not a ceiling — a smarter-than-average baseline still misses the same structural disciplines.

Eval-3 with_skill was the most expensive run (1521s, 180k tokens). The notebook format pulls the executor into more iteration rounds (jupytext conversion, code cell testing). If this becomes a concern, the skill could bundle a jupytext helper script to reduce round-trips.

Subagent permission inheritance is still flaky — 2 of 6 executors and 1 of 6 graders reported intermittent Write/Bash denials even after the allow-list expansion. Persistent subagents worked around it with python3 -c + pickle staging. This is a Claude Code harness issue, not a skill issue, and doesn't affect the quality signal.

Cleanest apples-to-apples comparison among the 3 evals: Eval-2, where with_skill and baseline differ by only 5 seconds and 2.5k tokens but the skill scores 10/10 vs 9/10. A pure quality win with essentially zero compute penalty.

Most defensible claim from this benchmark: the skill reliably produces audit-ready deliverables (validation.md, owners+confidence on every recommendation, action-titled charts) that a baseline analyst of equivalent capability consistently skips. The skill encodes discipline, not cleverness.
